title: Version constraints (^ ~ wildcards partials ||), fewest-candidates backtracking resolver with locks/yanks, install order with cycle members

hidden_checks.spec: Rule 3: ^P bounds for M > 0, ^0, ^0.m, ^0.0, ^0.0.p; rule 1 whitespace between operator and version.
Rule 3: ~P below M.(m+1).0 when m is given, else below (M+1).0.0.
Rule 3: *, M.*, M.m.*; =P / bare P: full exact, partial covers (1.2 = 1.2.*, =1 = 1.*).
Rules 2-3: >= floor, < floor, > partial = >= next-up, <= partial = < next-up, full versions strict/inclusive.
Rule 3: != is the negation of =P (partial and full); rule 1 terms in a group are ANDed.
Rule 1: || groups ORed, comma terms ANDed, whitespace ignored.
Rules 1 and 4: empty constraint/group/term, bad operators, operator with wildcard (incl. != with wildcard), ^*, ~*, inner wildcard, 4 parts, leading zeros, v prefix -> InvalidConstraint.
Constraint.allows accepts a Version or a version string.
Rule 7: candidates satisfy every active constraint, highest first; rule 8.
Rule 8: fewest candidates first, ties alphabetical; zero candidates fails and backtracks to the previous decision's next candidate.
Rule 8.2: choose the undecided package with the fewest candidates (y before x), which determines the chosen solution.
Rule 8.2: candidate counts are computed at each choice from the then-active requirements (r before q after p's decision).
Rule 8.2: ties on the candidate count go to the alphabetically smallest name; rule 9 requirement key order irrelevant.
Rule 8.4 chronological backtracking across several decisions; rule 9: packages only required by undone decisions are not in the result.
Rule 8.4: when the first choice fails, raise ResolutionError.
Rule 5: unknown root package -> UnknownPackage (a ResolutionError) with .name the alphabetically smallest.
Rule 7: an unknown package has no candidates, so the dependent version is abandoned (rule 8).
Rule 5: root requirements are parsed first; invalid -> InvalidConstraint.
Rule 7: yanked versions are excluded except the locked version, which is a candidate even if yanked.
Rule 7: the locked version is tried first when it exists and satisfies every active constraint; otherwise highest first.
Rule 7: a locked version failing an active constraint is not a candidate; locks for packages that are not required have no effect (rule 8.1 result = decided packages).
Rules 7 and 8.2: the locked (yanked) release counts as a candidate when choosing the next package; tie -> alphabetical.
Rule 8.3: a candidate whose dependency does not allow an already-decided version is skipped.
Rule 8.3: a dependency naming the package itself must allow the candidate.
Rule 9: result does not depend on registry insertion order or requirement key order.
Acceptance: pinwheel/install.py works unchanged (rules 8 and 10 via plan).
Rule 10: dependencies first; when several are ready, alphabetically smallest first.
Rule 10: only dependencies of the resolved version that are in the resolution count.
Rule 11: CycleError.members = sorted packages on at least one cycle (incl. self-dependency), not mere dependents.
Rule 11: members of a 3-cycle only; rule 10 ordering with another resolved version.
Rule 11: resolve does not reject cycles; install_order raises CycleError with the members.
